feature: Inspector numeric precision agrees with native input validity

finding.reproduction: Real Chromium marked the Inspector opacity value 0.75 invalid (`input.validity.valid === false`) because the number control declared step=0.1, while the same Inspector validator and shipped presets accept 0.75. The Browser value contract also accepts opacity 0.82, line-height 1.75 and scale 0.85, all valid decimals that do not land on a tenth.
finding.impact: A value that the Page Model accepts and the Canvas/public renderer uses was exposed to the browser and assistive technology as a step-invalid numeric control. This made the Inspector's native and application validation states disagree.
finding.fix: Numeric controls now use native step=any so every value accepted by the shared validator is valid in the browser. The declared registry step remains the ArrowUp/ArrowDown increment; custom keyboard handling applies that increment, clamps to the field contract bounds, and retains fractional preset values.
finding.reuse_review: The existing Property Registry contract and native number inputs remain in use. HTML number input validity and keyboard semantics were retained with native validity for arbitrary decimals and a small project-owned keyboard increment handler. No third-party code or new dependency was useful.
